creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`crates/muster-seam/src/session.rs` is 3853 lines holding two responsibilities that have nothing to do with each other, and it grows in both directions at once.

The first is launch-time configuration the shell hands over once at startup: roughly fifteen process-wide `static Mutex<Option<T>>` cells with a getter and a setter each, in lines ~50-306 - `DAEMON_BINARY`, `PLATFORM_LOCALE`, `COMMANDS`, `CACHE`, `STATE`, `NAMES_FILE`, `SHARED_NAMES`, `BINDINGS`, `PANE_INPUT`, `PANES`, `DAEMON_CONFIG`, `FEEL`, `CONFIG_PATH`, `APPEARANCE`, `PROBLEMS`.

The second is the `Session` struct and the live machinery around it - reconcile, publish, attach, the respawn record, the daemons a workspace has been asked of.

They share a file because there has never been another obvious home, so every new cross-cutting concern lands here. That is the cost: somebody changing either half has to hold all 3853 lines to be sure the other half is untouched.

Move the cells into a sibling module - `session/config.rs` or `startup.rs` - and leave `session.rs` as the struct plus its state machine.

## Not urgent, and not v0.4's doing

Raised by a maintainability review of the v0.4.0 diff (2026-09-01). The review found nothing else card-worthy in 5000 lines, and this predates v0.4: that release added `respawns` and `workspaces_asked_of` as `Session` fields, which is correctly scoped. v0.4 neither worsened this nor improved it.

## What done looks like

- The cells and their accessors live in their own module, with the file's own account of why launch config is a separate thing from a live session.
- `session.rs` is meaningfully shorter and reads as one subject.
- `./dev` green; no behaviour change, so no new cases.
title: 🧹 session.rs carries two unrelated things
